title: Caligula
objective: After this level you can separate what is known about Caligula from later rumor.
summary: Caligula, “little boot,” began popular in 37 CE and became autocratic. His own guard killed him in 41 CE. Many tales about him are hostile rumor.

cards.headline: Most of what you’ve heard about Caligula was written by people who hated him.
Little Boot
cards.body: Gaius, known as Caligula, became emperor in 37 CE. Caligula means “little boot,” a nickname soldiers gave him as a child, when he wore a small soldier’s uniform in his father’s camp. He was popular at first, but his rule soon became autocratic and extravagant.

cards.headline: Stories and evidence
cards.body: Most accounts of Caligula come from later writers hostile to him, so historians treat the wildest stories with caution. The tale that he planned to make his horse a consul may be a joke or an exaggeration.
cards.callout: Ask who wrote a story, and why

cards.fact: Caligula was murdered by officers of his own guard in 41 CE.
cards.context: The Praetorian Guard, meant to protect the emperor, ended his reign.

questions.prompt: What does the nickname Caligula mean?

options.label: Little soldier
options.rationale: Close, but it was about his footwear.

questions.explanation: Soldiers called the child Gaius “little boot” because of his small uniform.

questions.prompt: Why do historians doubt many stories about Caligula?

options.label: He banned all writing during his reign
The stories were all written in Greek
His coins show he was a gentle ruler
They come from later writers who hated him

questions.explanation: Hostile later writers had reasons to exaggerate, so their wildest claims need caution.

questions.prompt: From Level 51: which force, meant to protect the emperor, killed Caligula?
questions.explanation: Officers of the Praetorian Guard, stationed in Rome, murdered Caligula in 41 CE.
